findings.problem: LeaseWorkflow uses raw String for status and bool flags for is_validated/is_sent, allowing invalid state combinations (e.g. status="sent" with is_sent=false, or is_sent=true with sent_at_epoch_ms=None). No typestate or enum constrains the lifecycle.
findings.failure_mode: The struct can represent inconsistent lifecycle states that violate domain invariants. Callers cannot rely on status reflecting is_sent, and sent_at_epoch_ms may be None for a 'sent' lease.
findings.fix: Replace status: String with a sealed LeaseStatus enum (e.g. Pending, Validated, Sent) and replace is_validated/is_sent bools with typestate or derive them from the enum. Remove sent_at_epoch_ms or make it mandatory when status=Sent.

findings.problem: id is a raw String with no validation or newtype wrapping. Any string, including empty or malformed values, is accepted without boundary validation into the core.
findings.failure_mode: Core logic receives an invalid lease id that should have been rejected at the parse boundary, propagating bad data through the system.
findings.fix: Create a LeaseId newtype with a fallible constructor that rejects empty/malformed ids. Use LeaseId in LeaseWorkflow instead of String.

findings.problem: mark_sent mutates the struct in place and returns it, rather than being a pure function that constructs a new valid state from a well-typed input. No validation of preconditions (e.g. must be validated before sent).
findings.failure_mode: mark_sent can be called on any LeaseWorkflow regardless of current state, allowing transition from invalid states (e.g. unsanctioned status values, unvalidated items) into 'sent'.
findings.fix: Make mark_sent a pure function that takes a typed, validated input (e.g. LeaseWorkflow<LeaseStatus::Validated>) and returns LeaseWorkflow<LeaseStatus::Sent> with sent_at_epoch_ms populated. Use typestates or enum-based transitions to enforce allowed state changes.

findings.problem: status: String means every consumer must validate the string value to know the lease state. The core repeatedly validates primitives instead of accepting trusted domain types.
findings.failure_mode: Every branch of logic must re-check string equality for status, risking typos, case mismatches, and missed validations. Inconsistent branches can produce divergent behavior.
findings.fix: Replace status: String with a sealed LeaseStatus enum. Pattern-match on the enum instead of string comparison. Remove is_validated and is_sent as redundant boolean fields.

findings.problem: is_validated and is_sent are boolean lifecycle flags that should be a single enum or typestate. Two independent bools create 4 possible states, only some of which are valid.
findings.failure_mode: Invalid combinations like is_validated=true, is_sent=false (validating but not sending) or is_validated=false, is_sent=true (sending without validation) are constructable and have no domain meaning.
findings.fix: Replace is_validated and is_sent with a single LeaseStatus enum that enumerates valid lifecycle states: Pending, Validated, Sent. sent_at_epoch_ms becomes a field on the Sent variant only.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> allows None in all states. It should only be Some when the lease is in the Sent state, and None otherwise.
findings.failure_mode: A Sent lease can have sent_at_epoch_ms=None, making it impossible to determine when the lease was actually sent. Audit/logic relying on sent_at_epoch_ms will fail on valid structs.
findings.fix: Move sent_at_epoch_ms into the Sent variant of a LeaseStatus enum or use a typestate that only allows setting the timestamp when transitioning to Sent.

findings.problem: All fields of LeaseWorkflow are pub, allowing external code to mutate fields directly and bypass any invariants that mark_sent might enforce.
findings.failure_mode: External code can set item.status="sent" directly without calling mark_sent, skip sent_at_epoch_ms, and create an invalid struct without the function's logic running.
findings.fix: Make all fields private. Provide a sealed constructor (e.g. LeaseWorkflow::new) that enforces invariants, and expose only state-transition methods.

findings.problem: id: String is owned and heap-allocated. For an identifier, a newtype like LeaseId should be used, and the underlying storage should consider borrowed references or smaller representations.
findings.failure_mode: Every LeaseWorkflow carries a heap allocation for the id, even when only borrowed references are needed. No validation or semantic type for the id.
findings.fix: Replace String with a LeaseId newtype. Use &str or Cow<'_, str> at parse boundaries when lifetimes allow.

residual_risk: The LeaseWorkflow struct permits a combinatorial explosion of invalid states (invalid status strings, bool flag mismatches, missing sent timestamps, unchecked ids). Without typestates or enum-based lifecycle enforcement, any caller can construct an invalid LeaseWorkflow. Static review only; no commands run. The code shape requires a typestate/enum refactor before it can be trusted.
